title: Homelessness department: adopted budget against spending
question: How fast did the homelessness budget grow, and was the money spent?
finding: The homelessness department's adopted budget grew from $284.5 million in fiscal 2019 to $785.6 million in fiscal 2026; its spending grew from $233.7 million to $636.1 million. It spent less than its adopted budget in 7 of 8 years ($4.13 billion of $5.19 billion over the eight years), and less than its budgeted grants to providers in 7 of 8. The adopted budgets for fiscal 2027 and 2028 are $824.5 million and $772.0 million.
how: Department code HOM, all funds, all spending characters except transfers and transfer adjustments; adopted budget (xdgd-c79v) against the ledger (bpnb-jwfb).
limits: Project and grant budgets are multi-year: money budgeted and not spent in one year usually carries forward and is spent later, so a single year's gap is not money lost. The fiscal 2021 budget included tax money held back while the Proposition C lawsuit was pending. Payments recorded as grants in the ledger differ from the Controller's nonprofit payment file, which also counts contracts.
